div_boundary_F24.notes: At t>0 the window [t+2, t+4] runs past the trace end (t_max=2): clamping vs pessimistic boundary rules differ. Hero cell: Breach output must come from a real run (no recorded CSV exists for this case).

div_terminal_and.notes: Both signals violate only at the final sample; Breach extends the penultimate value of top-level and/or results over the terminal step. Hero cell: Breach output must come from a real run (no recorded CSV exists for this case).

div_interp_sparse.notes: Window falls entirely between sample points; piecewise-linear vs discrete sampling differ. Discrete tools cannot express the non-integer-multiple interval bounds: RTAMT discrete-time and STLCG++ are coverage '--'. Reuses the recorded Breach case interp_sparse (identical data).

div_nonuniform_always.notes: Non-uniform grid. Observed 2026-06-05: real RTAMT 0.3.5 does NOT raise; it silently treats the trace as uniform sample indices (out[i] = min(x[i], x[i+1])). The original trace (x[3]=4) made index semantics coincide with the piecewise-linear reading; x[3]=-2 separates them (PL [0,1,-1,-2,2] vs index [0,1,-2,-2,2], divergence at t=1.5). tidystl's rtamt backend instead REJECTS non-uniform grids -- a deliberate, documented coverage mismatch with the real tool, reported as such in the reproduction artifact. STLCG++ has no time vector -> coverage '--'. Breach cell needs the Day-3 run (the recorded nonuniform_always CSV has the pre-change trace).

div_equality.notes: Robustness of an equality predicate. Verified 2026-06-05: RTAMT 0.3.5 and STLCG++ 0.0.2 (Equal) both yield -|x-3|, matching tidystl on these samples. Re-verified on the live Breach run (1.11.4, MATLAB R2022b): contrary to the Day-2 assumption, Breach PARSES 'x[t] == 3' and returns BigM sign semantics (+/-10000), not a distance -- the cell is a genuine value divergence on the equality-predicate decision point, not a coverage gap.

div_until_boundary.notes: Tool-vs-tool divergence on a bounded until (= the E1 matrix cell until_boundary). On the 2-sample trace x=[5,-5], y=[-1,2], RTAMT reports +2 (SATISFIED) while Breach, TaLiRo, and STLCG++ all report -5 (VIOLATED): RTAMT is the lone outlier. The cause is RTAMT's discrete bounded-until composition at the trace boundary (the [1,2] window runs past the final sample), not anything visible in the syntax. The localizer pins every pairwise disagreement to the single U[1,2] operator (BoundedUntilKernel vs DiscreteBoundedUntil). No native baseline involved. Pure-numpy via tidystl_compat; no MATLAB / recorded CSV.

div_window_sampling.tidystl: G[0,3]( (mode >= 0) and F[0,1]( (enable >= 0) and G[1,2](level >= 0) ) ) and (safety_margin >= 0)
div_window_sampling.breach: alw_[0,3] ((mode[t] > 0) and ev_[0,1] ((enable[t] > 0) and alw_[1,2] (level[t] > 0))) and (safety_margin[t] > 0)
div_window_sampling.notes: Tool-vs-tool divergence buried at temporal nesting depth 3 (G[0,3] > F[0,1] > G[1,2]) on a NON-UNIFORM grid with a wide first segment [0,3] (samples only at t=0 and t=3). The buried G[1,2](level >= 0) reduces over a window lying entirely BETWEEN samples. Breach uses the interpolated predicate value at the window start -> +2; TaLiRo finds no sample inside the closed window and returns the always-identity (vacuously satisfied) -> the branch stays high. Both SATISFY the spec, but the root robustness differs: Breach +2.0 vs TaLiRo +5.0 -- a subtle value-only gap, no verdict flip, with no syntactic giveaway. The localizer isolates the single responsible operator G[1,2]. RTAMT and STLCG++ cannot run here (both reject non-uniform grids) -- itself a coverage finding; only the dense-time tools (Breach, TaLiRo) apply. No native baseline involved. Pure-numpy via tidystl_compat; no MATLAB / recorded CSV.
